'''John Allen Paulos''' (born July 4, 1945) is an American professor of [[mathematics]] at [[Temple University]] in [[Philadelphia]], [[Pennsylvania]], a writer and speaker on mathematics and the importance of [[numeracy|mathematical literacy]]. He writes about the dangers of mathematical [[innumeracy]], ie the layperson's misconceptions about numbers, probability, and logic.<ref name="MacNeal-1994">{{cite book |last=MacNeal |first=Edward |title=Mathsemantics: Making Numbers Talk Sense |date=1994 |publisher=Penguin |isbn=9780140234862 }}</ref>{{rp|133,213}}

==Early life==
Paulos was born in [[Denver Colorado|Denver, Colorado]] and grew up in Chicago, [[Illinois]] and [[Milwaukee]], [[Wisconsin]], where he attended high school. After his Bachelor of Mathematics at [[University of Wisconsin]] (1967) and his Master of Science at [[University of Washington]] (1968), he received his [[PhD]] in mathematics from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] (1974). In an interview he described himself as lifelong skeptic.<ref name="Podcast">{{cite web |title=Meet the Skeptics! |url=http://meettheskeptics.libsyn.com/mts-meet-john-allen-paulos |url-status=dead |publisher=Christopher Brown |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222062748/http://meettheskeptics.libsyn.com/mts-meet-john-allen-paulos |archivedate=February 22, 2014 |df=mdy-all}}</ref> He volunteered for the [[Peace Corps]] in the seventies.<ref>{{cite web|title=NNDB|url=http://www.nndb.com/org/786/000041663/|publisher=NNDB}}</ref>

==Career==

His academic work is mainly in [[mathematical logic]] and [[probability theory]].

His book ''[[Innumeracy (book)|Innumeracy: Mathematical Illiteracy and its Consequences]]'' (1988) was a bestseller and ''A Mathematician Reads the Newspaper'' (1995) extended the critique. In his books Paulos discusses [[innumeracy]] with quirky anecdotes, scenarios and facts, encouraging readers in the end to look at their world in a more [[quantitative property|quantitative]] way.

He has also written on other subjects often "combining disparate disciplines", such as the mathematical and philosophical basis of humor in ''Mathematics and Humor'' and ''I Think, Therefore I Laugh'', the [[stock market]] in ''A Mathematician Plays the Stock Market'', quantitative aspects of narrative in ''Once Upon a Number'', the arguments for God in ''Irreligion'', and most recently "bringing mathematics to bear on...biography" in ''A Numerate Life''.<ref>{{cite interview |last=Paulos |first=John Allen |interviewer=Jim Stein |title=A Numerate Life: A Mathematician Explores the Vagaries of Life, His Own and Probably Yours |url=http://newbooksinmath.com/2015/11/12/john-allen-paulos-a-numerate-life-prometheus-books-2015/ |date=10 November 2015 |work=New Books in Mathematics |access-date=24 January 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160115193717/http://newbooksinmath.com/2015/11/12/john-allen-paulos-a-numerate-life-prometheus-books-2015/ |archivedate=January 15, 2016 |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

Paulos also wrote a mathematics-tinged column for the UK newspaper ''[[The Guardian]]'' and is a [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry]] fellow.<ref>{{cite web|title=Committee for Skeptical Inquiry|url=http://www.csicop.org|publisher=CSI}}</ref>

Paulos has appeared frequently on radio and television, including a four-part [[BBC]] adaptation of ''A Mathematician Reads the Newspaper'' and appearances on the [[Lehrer News Hour]], [[20/20 (U.S. TV series)|20/20]], [[Larry King]], and [[David Letterman]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Paulos at David Letterman |url=https://math.temple.edu/~paulos/other.html |publisher=Temple University |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20010411001818/http://www.math.temple.edu/~paulos/other.html |archivedate=April 11, 2001 }}</ref>

In 2001 Paulos taught a course on quantitative literacy for journalists at the Columbia University School of Journalism. The course stimulated further programs at Columbia and elsewhere in precision and data-driven journalism.{{citation needed|date=September 2016}}

His long-running "[[ABCNews.com]]" monthly column ''Who's Counting''<ref name="Who's Counting">[https://abcnews.go.com/Technology/WhosCounting/ Who's Counting] at ABC News</ref> deals with mathematical aspects of stories in the news. All the columns over a 10- year period are archived here.<ref name="Who's Counting"/>

== Private life ==
He is married, father of two, grandfather of four.

==Awards==

* 2013: JPBM ([[Joint Policy Board for Mathematics]]) Award for communicating mathematics on a sustained basis to large audiences<ref>{{cite web|title=JPBM Award for Communicating Mathematics|url=http://math.mit.edu/mathcomm/archives/john-allen-paulos-to-receive-math-communications-award/|publisher=JPBM}}</ref>
* 2003: AAAS ([[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]) Award for promoting the public understanding of science and technology<ref>{{cite web|title=AAAS|url=http://www.aaas.org/aboutaaas/awards/public/public2003.shtml|publisher=AAAS|access-date=March 14, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130516041142/http://www.aaas.org/aboutaaas/awards/public/public2003.shtml|archive-date=May 16, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 2002: University Creativity Award at [[Temple University]]<ref>{{cite web|title=University Creativity Award|url=http://www.temple.edu/provost/faculty/awards/research-and-creative.html|publisher=Temple University}}</ref>
* 1994: Folio Award for the article ''Counting on Dyscalculia'' which appeared in ''Discover Magazine'' in 1994<ref>{{cite web|title=Discover Magazine|url=http://discovermagazine.com/1994/mar/countingondyscal351#.UqCSc8RDsvw|publisher=Discover Magazine}}</ref>
